$about: Cassette player kit tokens: ONE source for the iPhone app, the Android app, the desktop app and the web player. Values are lifted from the iPhone app, which is the reference (AmperfyKit/CassetteTokens.swift, CassetteTheme.swift, CassetteFont.swift, CassetteIcons.swift and the screens named in each component's `ios` field). Sizes are points on iOS and Android and CSS pixels on the web. Run `pnpm --filter @discovery/cassette-kit generate` after any change: it writes src/tokens.module.css (web), generated/CassetteKitTokens.swift and generated/CassetteKitTokens.kt. Each colour role carries its value for the light paper (`light`), for a surface whose paper follows the reader's device (the web's `.follow` beside `.kit`, the desk today): a hex, or for the two orange roles `deepen`, the share of black mixed into the skin's orange so it still holds on cream (0.12 for a bar, 0.31 for type). A role without one (the record tints but their text) is the same on both. Every light text role reads 4.5:1 or better on every light surface. `fillSelected` is the one primary fill (Play, Resume, a switch's lit choice, the transport's play, a tile's play): on the light paper an espresso rather than the ink, so the big ones aren't holes in the page, deepening to the ink when pointed at (the founder, 2026-10-29). `shape` is a corner as a share of the side, for a part whose corner grows with it: a station's own mark (its logo or its word art) is rounded at 22.5% of its side, the app icon's shape, wherever it stands for the station, on every platform (the founder: 2026-10-22 on the Mac, 2026-10-29 for the phones); what a station is playing (a show's picture, a record) keeps a cover's corners.

fillHover.ios: web only: a selected fill pointed at

answer.note: New York is Apple's own face and only ships on Apple platforms; Android and the web use Newsreader italic in its place.

icon.$note: Each concept names its Lucide glyph (iOS draws the cassette-lucide-<name> asset; Android and the web draw Lucide). Transport glyphs are SF Symbols on iOS only; elsewhere the kit's own filled shapes. SF Symbols may not ship off Apple platforms.

images.$about: The image ladder: every picture Cassette shows comes in these sizes and no others (docs/reference/CASSETTE_IMAGES.md; plan in docs/CASSETTE_IMAGE_LADDER_PLAN.md). A rung is the longest side in pixels of a box the stored size fits inside, keeping the picture's shape; nothing is ever enlarged. Catalog and uploaded pictures are served at `host` + `path` (WebP, made once by services/media-edge; bucket `m` is the media bucket, `u` the uploads bucket, `x` an outside original on one of `externalHosts`, base64url-encoded); a person's own pictures come from their hub at the same rungs. `pick` is the rule every platform runs, generated into Swift and Kotlin from this file and checked against `pickExamples` on each: frame width and height in points, the screen's scale, the picture's aspect (width over height; covers 1, photos assumed 1.5 when unknown), `cover` (crops to fill) or `contain`, and the picture's natural longest side when known. Adding a rung is cheap; changing or removing one moves every stored size, so it is the founder's call.

pickExamples.why: a song row on a phone
a 3:2 photo filling a circle needs its short side to cover
a wide banner cropping a square cover
past the top rung stays at the top
never ask above the picture's own size
a tiny picture asks for the rung that holds it

taste.$about: The web's taste roles (the cassette.digital pages: the homepage, artist, album, apps, and every page in the taste page frame). The web reads them from src/taste.module.css, which apps/cassette's _taste/taste.module.css composes; the native files carry them as CassetteKitTokens.Taste. One founder call is a switch here, a word: `skins` is what an account skin moves on these pages ("accent": only the orange, as built; "paper": the stocks turn with the site's neutral dial too, as the desk does). Corners are settled (the founder, 2026-10-29, round everywhere): anything you press, anything you type into and every tag is round (`pill`, a capsule, or a circle when it holds only an icon); a box that holds a paragraph takes `area`; rows, strips, code and other small boxes take `small`; cards `card`; covers `cover`. The old `corners` switch is retired and the generator refuses it. The `button` role is the player kit's own `pill` type (read from there, so both kits set a button the same way); `link` keeps the typewriter letters for arrow links. A control's height and outline come from the kit's `component.pill`. No type role is ever set under `floor` pixels: the generator refuses one. Inside the iPhone app's web views (html[data-surface="app"], set before paint by apps/cassette lib/app-surface.ts) the floor is `appFloor`: every role under it is raised to it there (the founder's Decision 4, 2026-10-29: 13px in the iPhone's web pages, 11px stays on the website, and the desktop app stays on 11 until someone measures it). `fill` is a primary button's fill (a filled button, a lit chip, the dock's play): the ink on the dark stock, and on the light one the same espresso as the player kit's `fillSelected`, so every light-mode primary is one dark (the founder, 2026-10-29). `danger` is the ink for something that went wrong (a form error), text-safe on the stock and on its raised surface; it is not a second orange. A stock can name its own lowest text step (`ink3`) where the shared `inkSteps` one reads under 4.5:1 on its paper: the light stock does (0.56 read 4.1:1 on its cream; 0.62 reads 4.7:1 or better on every light surface, the sleeve included).

cs.$about: The old web kit's role names (apps/cassette globals.css, --cs-*) written from the taste roles, for a page still drawn in the old kit inside the taste page frame: its parts then draw in the taste inks, corners and type sizes with no change of their own. Each name points at a stock role (color), a corner (radius) or a type role's size (size).
